title.narrative: CRTA 2022-2026: civil society for democracy and EU, Serbia
CRTA 2022-2026: civilsamhället för demokrati och EU, Serbien

description.narrative: 2.1The overall objectives of the Core Activities as stated in its Strategic Plan are: CRTA vision: "Serbia with established social and political consensus about the European Union as a partner and EU membership as a defined national interest. Acknowledged firm and unambiguous strategic orientation of the country to develop democracy and political culture, opens society towards European, democracy and human rights values, where citizens are active and persistent in demanding and defending accountable governance." CRTAs strategic commitment for the period 2022-2027 is to contribute in preventing further democratic backsliding and to support creating conditions for developing democratic values and protecting the public interest: 1. CRTA contributes to creating social resiliency against undemocratic and disinformation influences, leading to a more informed and pluralistic society aspiring toward the EU. - Citizens and various stakeholders are provided with access to verified and truthful information on issues of public importance, particularly those related to accountable governance and the rule of law. - CRTA aims to support solidarity and joint actions of civil society initiatives in Serbia in defending the public interest and promoting democratic and European values and to equip and protect them with tools and resources for resisting pressures on their work. - CRTA aims to educate and engage different social groups and professions, including journalists, civic activists, youth, and academia in disclosing and combating undemocratic mechanisms, including disinformation. 2. CRTA contributes to establishing a foundation for institutional accountability, transparency and openness, increasing citizen trust in a democratic perspective. - CRTA is recognized as a credible democracy watchdog by Serbias citizens and democratic actors. - Domestic stakeholders and decision-makers are provided with concrete recommendations and roadmaps for policies that ensure the state's democratic performance and protect the public interest. - Citizens of Serbia recognize the importance of democratic institutions and are encouraged to raise demand for institutional accountability. - International stakeholders interested and engaged in supporting democratic development in Serbia are provided with evidence-based assessments of the state of democracy in Serbia.
Core support to CRTA 2022-2026 and their overal Startegic Plan with narrow focus in the first year on combating disinformation.

description.narrative:
CRTAs observation mission around December 2023 elections provided a detailed insight into the electoral processes and activities in Serbia, enabling the overall, evidence-based assessment of the quality of elections conduct, provision of sound argumentation and evidence on electoral manipulations and breaches, and efforts to safeguard the integrity of elections and citizens voting rights. Electoral insights documented by CRTA have fed into the ODIHR election observation reports and recommendations, ensuring broader demand for resolution of electoral breaches in the country.
CRTAs election observation findings were crucial in providing decision makers, both domestic and international, with substantial evidence and argumentation regarding the integrity of electoral conduct. They have been largely used as evidence by international observers, domestic political parties, civil society actors active in electoral field, as well as the high-level decision makers demanding the resolution of documented electoral breaches (European Economic and Social Council, Monitoring Committee of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, Bundestag, State Department etc.).
CRTAs recognition of relevant civil society and advocacy actor in the electoral area has also been proved through the invitation to provide contribution and propose concrete measures for resolution of electoral breaches, and to participate in discussions between ruling and opposition parties, organized by the Parliament regarding electoral conditions and ODIHR recommendations. CRTA has also been included into the working groups for verification of the Voter Registry and amending electoral laws, proving its credibility, and raising the potential for its higher influence on the improvement of electoral conditions in longer term.
CRTAs electoral advocacy efforts gained notable momentum in 2024. As an active member of the parliamentary Working Group for the Improvement of the Electoral Process, CRTA contributed concrete policy solutions aimed at reinforcing electoral oversight and restoring public confidence. Among the most notable contributions was CRTAs legislative proposal on Voter Registry Audit, positively assessed by the OSCEs ODIHR, which emphasized its credibility and policy relevance in democratic reform debates.
Further strengthening its public positioning, CRTA organized the high-profile international conference In Effect, Do We Elect?, which convened leading experts, civil society organizations and institutional actors to examine electoral integrity and discuss ways to counter Serbias democratic erosion. These spaces served as a nexus for cross-sectoral dialogue on elections.
CRTAs observation mission around the June 2024 Belgrade elections represented the comprehensive civil society-led electoral assessments in Serbia. The mission documented persistent electoral abuses, including voter intimidation, manipulative voter migration and misuse of public functions, and produced evidence-based findings that have been widely used in domestic and international policy arenas.
These findings were reflected in major institutional documents, including the European Parliaments Resolution of February 8, 2024 and the OSCE/ODIHR Final Report of February 28, 2024, both of which echoed CRTAs key observations. The reach of these reports underscored CRTAs influence in shaping both public understanding and institutional approaches to electoral integrity in Serbia.
Through sustained monitoring of parliamentary activities, CRTA continued to document the proceedings within the National Assembly. The Open Parliament initiative, along with regular analysis and publication, ensured continuous scrutiny of legislative performance and promoted accountability for elected officials.
In parallel with institutional monitoring, CRTA maintained a strong presence in the public sphere through data-driven campaigns, digital outreach and accessible content. Despite political pressures and restricted media space, CRTAs communications strategy ensured its messages and findings reached wide and diverse audiences, particularly younger demographics and politically engaged citizens.
RTAs thematic campaigns contributed to public education, civic mobilization and increased demand for institutional accountability, while strengthening its reputation as a credible voice in public discourse. A large following of loyal and active users indicates that users actively and continually engage with CRTAs research by downloading, reading reports or subscribing to newsletters, while new users show a comparably high level of audience growth which are both illustrative of a stable, rising demand for a democratic culture. CRTAs public recognition is further observable through the growing number of media mentions, reflected in a 34% increase in relation to 2023 and a 54% increase in relation to 2022.
CRTAs integrated fact-checking and media monitoring efforts continued to combat the normalization of falsehoods and disinformation in the Serbian media environment. Through Istinomer and other tools, CRTA equipped citizens and journalists with timely analyses that dissected media narratives, debunked manipulation and exposed the role of political and foreign actors in shaping public perception.
In addition, CRTAs public opinion research served as a critical resource for both domestic and international stakeholders to better understand citizens perceptions of democracy, institutional trust and political participation.
